result.summary: Adds a unit test in `fs_tests` verifying that `std::filesystem::copy_file` with `copy_options::overwrite_existing` successfully overwrites an existing file. This tests for an upstream libstdc++ bug on Windows where `copy_file` throws a "File exists" error despite the overwrite flag.
result.problem: Certain versions of GCC libstdc++ on Windows have an upstream bug where `copy_file` fails when attempting to overwrite an existing destination file. Production code such as `BerkeleyRODatabase::Backup()` in the wallet migration logic relies on `overwrite_existing` working, but there was no unit test catching affected toolchain environments.
evidence: The PR description links CI build logs reproducing the failure during cross-compilation for Windows with GCC 14.2.0: 'std::filesystem::__cxx11::filesystem_error: filesystem error: cannot copy file: File exists'
The description identifies wallet migration code (`src/wallet/migrate.cpp`'s `BerkeleyRODatabase::Backup()`) that relies on `overwrite_existing` working correctly
result.scope_notes: A small test-only addition (+26 lines) to `test/fs_tests.cpp`.
result.card: Adds a unit test in fs_tests to check whether std::filesystem::copy_file functions with the overwrite_existing flag. Upstream GCC libstdc++ on Windows contains a bug where copy_file throws a filesystem error claiming the file exists even when overwrite_existing is requested. Wallet migration relies on this operation in BerkeleyRODatabase::Backup, and CI logs confirm the test catches toolchains affected by the bug.

risk.why: Only adds a unit test in fs_tests; a failure would only fail CI or unit tests on affected toolchains.
